idiom_name: free function per request + RAII transaction guard (scope_exit / scope_fail)
implementation_notes: The class-per-script structure is mostly unnecessary in C++: a free function in a namespace per subject area takes the request parameters plus a database/transaction object, and RAII expresses the transaction boundary instead of a manual try/catch pair. A scope guard (std::experimental::scope_exit, the C++26 std::scope_exit from P0052, or a small hand-rolled guard) registers the rollback unconditionally and the success path disarms it with release(), so every early return and every exception rolls back without extra code - the guard replaces the begin/commit bookkeeping the classic script writes by hand. Keep the script free of presentation code and push SQL into a thin gateway (or a library such as SOCI). The classic form is still justified when scripts must be stored, queued or decorated as objects (Command style), for example in job or undo systems.
pitfalls: Ordering bug: commit() must be the last fallible operation before release(); an exception thrown after commit() leaves an armed guard that rolls back an already committed transaction.
The guard's callable runs during stack unwinding, so it must be noexcept - a throwing rollback calls std::terminate.
A guard holding a lambda that captures by reference must not outlive the referenced locals; returning or storing it is a dangling-reference bug.
